### 2026-10-11 – Timelapse of my second Starbie work session (about 4 hours total, first 2 recorded).

**4.33h**

Timelapse of my second Starbie work session (about 4 hours total, first 2 recorded).

In the first hour I finished building out the schematic: I added the two buttons, the screen connector, the MPU6050 connector and the DHT11 sensor with its 10k pull-up resistor, and connected everything to the XIAO ESP32-C3 with wires and net labels. Then I opened the PCB Editor for the first time, brought my parts in and drew a star-shaped board outline.

In the second hour I went back and rechecked my connections against the guide's pictures and fixed the errors I found, like labels that weren't actually attached to a pin and an error about the XIAO when I updated the PCB from the schematic.

During these two hours I went slower than I had to. The guide tells you what to do, but I wanted to understand what each part is for, so I spent time learning about each one as I added it.

The recording stopped working after about 2 hours and I didn't notice until I reached a stopping point at around 4 hours. In those last two unrecorded hours I started putting the wiring together on the board, connecting the parts and getting more comfortable with the software.

[Timelapse](https://lookout.hackclub.com/api/media/e2fce02f-bd35-4141-bd2f-0d325f3c0cc3/video.mp4)

### 2026-10-11 – Finished my Starbie! In these 5 hours I routed the last tracks, added a ground fill and got my design check down from 10 errors to the 2 the guide says are okay (one track was on the wrong pad and sho

**5h**

Finished my Starbie! In these 5 hours I routed the last tracks, added a ground fill and got my design check down from 10 errors to the 2 the guide says are okay (one track was on the wrong pad and shorting two signals). Then I added my Attack on Titan silkscreen art and my name to the board. After that I set up Arduino IDE, matched the pin numbers in the code to my board, made my own 32x32 pet sprite, named it Totoro and added a sparkle trail. I fixed a few compile errors along the way, exported my Gerbers and put everything on GitHub with a README. Everything was new to me but it's done!
